blocks.text: Audience: developers who write docs with coding agents (repo-docs seed). Style: YC launch video — real pixels, no music, one CTA. Concrete subject throughout: a real file (`design-doc.md`), a real elapsed time (three days), a real diff stat — never an abstract "docs."

| Time | Screen | Narration |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:14 | `design-doc.md` on a GitHub PR page, three days of commits, diff stat reading **+1,204 −980** | I kept asking my agent to fix a design doc. Three days later, all GitHub showed me was a thousand-line diff. I couldn't tell what changed, why, or how to get back to an earlier draft. |
| 0:14–0:24 | Cut to black-on-white statement card | So I gave markdown its own git — one that lives right inside the repo you already have. Introducing Proofpress: every edit, yours or your agent's, becomes a version — what changed, why, and a way back. |
| 0:24–0:42 | Split screen: same three days as a nine-commit git log (vague messages) vs. Proofpress version chain, each version tagged with its reason | Same three days, two views. Git: a thousand lines of noise across nine commits nobody opened. Proofpress: one section moved, one paragraph rewritten, one number changed — every round, one glance, reason attached. Verified against what actually changed — the agent can't oversell its work. |
| 0:42–0:53 | Open the PR: the proofpress bot comment — block-level change list + "✅ claims verified (deterministic check)"; then a manual hand-edit landing in the same chain | Open the pull request — Proofpress already commented: what moved, what was rewritten, and whether the agent's own changelog survives a deterministic check. Edit the file yourself instead — same ledger, same history, either way. |
| 0:53–1:00 | Logo + tagline + repo URL | Draft → Review → Approve, for agents. Open source. Link below. |

~155 words. Delivery notes: speak slowly (reviewers watch at 2×); on-screen diff stat can carry precise-looking numbers (+1,204 −980) even where narration rounds them off for spoken flow ("a thousand-line diff") — screen and voice don't have to match digit-for-digit. Narration never describes what's on screen — it adds the judgment layer on top.

Red-line check: no mention of versioning code files; no review-of-humans language; "git" appears only as contrast/metaphor, never as the thing being replaced — Proofpress lives inside git, it doesn't compete with it.

> I kept asking my coding agent to fix a doc. Three days later, all GitHub showed me was a 1,000-line diff — I couldn't tell what actually changed, why, or how to get back to an earlier draft.
>
> So I gave markdown its own git — one that lives right inside the repo you already have.
>
> Introducing Proofpress: every markdown edit, yours or your agent's, becomes a version — what changed, why, and a way back.
**Thread (optional, if expanding past the single post):**

> Same three days, two views.
>
> Git: a thousand lines of noise across nine commits nobody opened.
> Proofpress: one section moved, one paragraph rewritten, one number changed — every round, one glance, reason attached.
>
> The agent's changelog is verified against the real diff. It can't oversell its work.

> Open the PR and Proofpress has already commented: every block that moved or was rewritten — and a deterministic check that the agent's changelog matches what actually changed. Every version records who, why, and what was considered and rejected.
>
> Three weeks later, the answer's still there.

> Draft → Review → Approve, for agents.
>
> One skill for your agent, or one GitHub Action for the whole team. No new editor, no migration — your agent already writes markdown, this just keeps the books.
>
> Apache-2.0. [github link]
